messages.author: 54c05e928c45ac6c
messages.subject: Re: Is there any solution to improve factor loading?
parts:
What do you mean by "too low?" There is no such thing as "improving" factor loadings - they are one of the infinite solutions to the factor analytic problem.

If your concern is that some items have low loadings when you think they should have high loadings (relative to others), you may have misspecified the factor structure - in essence, your latent factor isn't measuring what you expect it to capture. Alternatively, you have non-classically noisy items or are mistaken about their importance.

In any case, it is fine to have items with low loadings and in some cases dropping them can change the substantive interpretation of your factor(s). That being said, extremely low loadings (e.g. standardized 0.01) almost always suggest some sort of error or misunderstanding.
